purpose: Prevent copy-paste operator commands from being corrupted, closing the interactive shell, relying on an unverified remote file/ref, or depending on an executable that exists but cannot actually launch.

directories.purpose: Command-delivery maps, workflows, fixtures, report template, and opt-in hook.
Scoped procedure for producing and verifying copy-paste operator commands.
PowerShell completeness validator and concrete child-executable launch probe.
Human-readable command-delivery state and recovery guide.

commands.name: Concrete executable launch

knownTraps: PowerShell environment references are $env:NAME. A backslash before the colon, such as $env\:TEMP, is command corruption and must fail validation.
Do not paste prompt markers, PS C:\ prompts, continuation prompts, transcript decorations, or escaped URL punctuation into operator commands.

A top-level exit in an interactive PowerShell command can close the operator terminal and destroy visible diagnostics. Run exit-propagating work in a child process and print the captured exit code in the parent shell.
Remote GitHub content must not be treated as present merely because a commit or PR was reported. Resolve the ref and the exact file through a read request before handing off the command.
For gh api content retrieval with parameters, use an explicit GET request and field argument instead of depending on an interpolated query string.

where, Get-Command, file existence, download success, and remembered version data do not prove an executable can launch. Concretely start the exact executable with UseShellExecute=false and bounded safe arguments before downstream runtime work depends on it.
Access is denied before the downstream artifact exists is a child-executable-launch failure, not evidence that the downstream runtime or tmux failed.
Generated runtime evidence remains outside the repository and must not be committed.
Static command validation and child-launch proof do not prove target runtime, GUI visibility, tmux attachment, provider authentication, or operator acceptance.
proofCeiling: Tracked command-delivery contracts, deterministic corruption detection, source-resolution requirements, concrete bounded child-executable launch proof, safe interactive-shell semantics, and CI validation. Live downstream operator execution remains separate runtime proof.
